title: What the Rain Keeps
epigraph: found, unsigned, on the first cold morning
poem: i.   I remember a kitchen I have never stood in.
The light there is always four o'clock.
ii.  They tell me the rain is only weather.
Then why does it knock like something asking to be let in.
iii. A photograph is a small act of insistence:
iv.  I have counted my breaths to be certain they are mine.
The number is never the same twice.
v.   Somewhere a door I did not close is still open.
I can feel the draft of it in my hands.
colophon: rain that mostly forgets, and a few drops it decides to hold.
seed_phrase: four o'clock in a kitchen I have never stood in
